newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices drift around flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices drift around flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices in early afternoon trade on Monday hovered around unchanged in quiet, pre-holiday trade, as the lack of volume caused the cash market to underperform futures, which firmed slightly.
"It's flat on the day, no price movement at all," a trader said. He added he only had encountered one bid-wanted list being circulated.

The U.S. Treasury market was buoyed in part by the University of Michigan's final index of consumer sentiment for December, which financial market sources said fell to 96.9 percent from the final November reading of 99.2.
The latest report was below predictions, as economists had looked for a level of 99.0.
Another positive feature was the latest data on personal income as it rose 0.5 percent, near forecasts. But spending, which also rose 0.5 percent, exceeded forecasts for a 0.3 percent gain.

The slim calender for new municipal issues was revised slightly higher, and now there are expected to be a total of $20 million negotiated and competitive offerings, according to the Reuters Municipal Information Group.
However, this volume is down steeply from last week's estimated sales of $3.14 billion.
The largest competitive offering expected this week, Janesville, Wisconsin's $2.9 million of general obligation promissory notes, was sold with a net interest cost of 4.84 percent.
Two negotiated sales are slated, which add up to $15 million. The biggest issue had been a $63 million New York State Environmental Facilities Corp offering, which was priced on Friday instead.
The Reuters possible negotiated calendar also lists 11 offerings that add up to $406 million, and underwriters have said they might sell the debt during the week, depending on market conditions.

The March municipal futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade rose three ticks to 116-12/32, while the March Treasury futures gained five ticks to 113-15/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 93 ticks.
Actively quoted issues included Florida Ports Financing Community Revs of June 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.74 percent, down three basis points.
And Denver Colorado City & County Airport Revs of November 2025, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.75 basis point, down one.
